info.title: Ecom & FileManager API Documentation
info.description:
Documentation of every API endpoint of the Ecom web application (port 3000) and the FileManager microservice (port 4000). Server-rendered HTML pages are out of scope, apart from the few read-only ones described under Response conventions.

### Base URLs
- Web application: `http://localhost:3000`
- FileManager microservice: `http://localhost:4000` (operations under `/files` and `/folders` are served only there)

### Authentication
- **Customer** and **admin** JSON endpoints (`/api`, `/admin/api`) accept either the HTTP-only cookie (`tokenUser`, `tokenAdmin`), which browsers use, or `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`, which API clients use. The login endpoints return `accessToken` in the body and set the cookie; a request that carries an `Authorization` header is authenticated by it alone and its cookies are ignored. The token lasts one day (`expiresIn` says how long); there is no refresh for Bearer clients, so log in again on 401.
- **FileManager** `/files` and `/folders` endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <FILE_MANAGER_SECRET>`. `/media` is public. Use a random secret of at least 32 characters; repeated wrong secrets from one address are answered with HTTP 429.
- Admin endpoints also check a permission (shown on each operation). Every admin write is recorded in the admin activity log.

### Trying requests
The Web application serves this documentation itself at `/api-docs/`, which is the place to try customer and admin endpoints: log in through the login endpoint (the cookie is then sent automatically), or paste the returned `accessToken` under "Authorize". The Web application sends CORS headers on non-admin routes, so the Vercel copy can reach storefront endpoints with a Bearer token; admin endpoints skip CORS on purpose, so try those from this same-origin copy instead. The FileManager bearer endpoints also work from the Vercel copy when FileManager lists its origin in `FILE_MANAGER_CORS_ORIGINS`.

### Response conventions
- A successful JSON response has HTTP 200 and `{ "code": "success", "message": "...", ...data }`.
- An error has the matching HTTP status and `{ "code": "error", "message": "..." }`: **400** invalid request, **401** not logged in, **403** no permission or not allowed, **404** record not found, **409** conflict with the current state (duplicate value, missing stock, a change that is not allowed), **429** too many attempts (see `Retry-After`), **500** unexpected failure, **502** a service the application depends on (FileManager, email, the shipping carrier) failed, and **503** the store is not fully configured yet for the request (for example, checkout without a warehouse location set).
- JSON endpoints (`/api`, `/admin/api`) never redirect: without a valid login they answer 401, and without the permission 403, whatever the method. Server-rendered page requests are redirected (302) to the login page, unless they send an `Authorization` header, `Accept: application/json` without `text/html`, or `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, which get the same 401 or 403 as the JSON endpoints. FileManager answers 401 when the bearer secret is missing or wrong.
- The storefront is server-rendered. The few page routes that act as read endpoints (catalog, articles, cart, flagged orders, payment and OAuth redirects) are documented with `text/html` or redirect responses; the other pages are not part of the API.
- JSON endpoints are plural resources under `/api` (storefront) and `/admin/api` (admin). The HTTP method states the action: `POST` creates, `PUT` and `PATCH` change, `DELETE` removes, and `GET` never changes data. Payment-gateway and OAuth callbacks keep the URLs their providers call.
- Trash lifecycle of admin resources: `DELETE /{id}` moves a record to the trash, `POST /{id}/restore` restores it and `DELETE /{id}?permanent=true` deletes it for good. The bulk variants take `{ "ids": [...] }` on the collection: `POST /trash`, `POST /restore` and `DELETE /`.

### Optional modules
Each store switches optional modules on or off with `FEATURE_*` environment variables (see the Ecom README). An endpoint of a switched-off module answers **404** like a route that does not exist: chat (`/api/chat-rooms`, `/admin/api/chat-rooms`), AI chat helpers, flagged orders, recommendation jobs, blog (`/api/articles`, `/api/article-categories`, `/admin/api/articles`, `/admin/api/article-categories`), wishlist, compare, reviews (`/api/reviews`, `/admin/api/reviews`), coupons (`/api/coupon-checks`, `/admin/api/coupons`; checkout then refuses a coupon with 400) and loyalty points (checkout ignores `usePoint`).

### Real-time chat (Socket.IO, same origin as the Web app)
Connect with the auth cookie and `auth: { role: "user" | "admin", roomId? }`.
- Client to server: `CLIENT_SEND_MESSAGE`, `CLIENT_TYPING`, `CLIENT_OPEN_CHAT`, `CLIENT_DELETE_MESSAGE`, `ADMIN_OPEN_CHAT`, `ADMIN_TYPING`, `ADMIN_DELETE_ROOM`.
- Server to client: `SERVER_SEND_MESSAGE`, `SERVER_SEND_STATUS`, `SERVER_MESSAGE_DELIVERED`, `SERVER_DELETE_MESSAGE`, `SERVER_DELETE_ROOM`, `SERVER_ROOM_ASSIGNED`, `SERVER_SEND_CLIENT_TYPING`, `SERVER_SEND_ADMIN_TYPING`, `SERVER_CLIENT_READ`, `SERVER_ADMIN_READ`, `SERVER_ADMIN_STATUS`, `USER_STATUS_ONLINE`, `LIST_USER_ONLINE`.

headingFont.description: A Google Fonts family name; empty keeps the theme font.

bodyFont.description: A Google Fonts family name; empty keeps the theme font.

displayCurrencies.description: ISO 4217 codes shoppers may view prices in, as a list or comma-separated text.

locale.description: BCP 47 locale for numbers and dates, e.g. vi-VN.

moneyPerPoint.description: Order value that earns one loyalty point.

pointValue.description: Discount one loyalty point is worth.

id.description: Pass it back as `shippingMethod` when placing the order ("<provider>:<rate>").

expected.description: Expected delivery time as the carrier words it.

cart.description: The cart lines with current product details and quantities capped at the stock.

shippingOptions.description: Cheapest first. Carriers that price by address (GoShip) appear only once `userAddress` is sent.

redirectUrl.description: Where to send the customer next, the order summary or the payment gateway start page.

accessToken.description: JWT for `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is also set in the HttpOnly cookie, which is what browsers use.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires. There is no refresh for Bearer clients: log in again on 401.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request: validation failed or the input is malformed.

Unauthorized.description: Not logged in. Page requests are redirected to the login page instead.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, for example a duplicate value, missing stock or a change that is not allowed.

BadGateway.description: A service the application depends on (FileManager, email, GoShip) failed.

RedirectToLogin.description: Not logged in; redirected to the login page.

PermissionDenied.description: The admin lacks the permission, or the action is not allowed for this account. API calls get `{ "code": "error", "message": "..." }`; page requests get an HTML 403 page.

RateLimited.description: Too many attempts. The `Retry-After` header holds the seconds to wait; the body is `{ "code": "error", "message": "..." }`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

UploadRejected.description: Invalid request, or the upload was rejected (type, size or file count).

FileManagerBadRequest.description: Invalid request or the operation failed.

TooManyFailedAttempts.description: Too many failed bearer attempts from this address; retry after the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header. Requests with the correct secret are never blocked.

FileManagerForbidden.description: Path outside the media root or not allowed.

FileManagerConflict.description: A file or folder with that name already exists.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The store is not fully configured yet (warehouse location, sender phone or address missing in Settings > General), so the request cannot be completed.
